acceptedFindings.title: Complete omission of ANCOVA results
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A research article must present its main findings: F‑test for group effect, p‑value, adjusted means, and confidence intervals. Without these, the study is unreportable.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the full ANCOVA table from stats-run.json in the manuscript, including sum of squares, F‑statistic, p‑value, and adjusted group means with their standard errors.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Manuscript text contains only the sample size; no mention of the ANCOVA p‑value (0.114) or any effect estimates. Compare with stats-run.json which holds all computed values.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing study design, data source, and eligibility criteria
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot assess generalizability, selection bias, or reproducibility. The cohort construction process (e.g., exclusions, missing data handling) is entirely opaque.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a detailed Methods section describing the data source (origin, time frame, sampling), inclusion/exclusion criteria, and how 240 complete cases were obtained from the larger dataset.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Manuscript only states 'cohort definition was read from available run artifacts' without any actual description; the required details are absent.

acceptedFindings.title: Variables undefined
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: No definition of outcome_cont, group, age, or severity is provided. Units, measurement method, and reference category for group are unknown, making the study impossible to interpret clinically.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a table or text defining each variable, including its role (outcome, exposure, covariate), how it was measured, its range, and for group, specify the categories and which is the reference level.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Manuscript notes that variables were 'not fully encoded' and defers to a companion artifact that is not supplied; no variable definitions appear.

acceptedFindings.title: Results section contains no statistical output
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript does not answer the study question; critical model estimates, p-values, and effect sizes are absent, rendering it useless for interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report all ANCOVA terms: group effect (F(2,235)=2.19, p=0.114), covariate effects, model fit, and ideally adjusted means and contrasts.

acceptedFindings.title: Prespecified study question is never stated
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot assess whether the analysis addresses a meaningful hypothesis or aligns with the objective.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the study question in the Introduction, and explain how the ANCOVA model was chosen to answer it.

acceptedFindings.title: No baseline characteristics table
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a table of covariate means (or medians) by group, readers cannot judge covariate imbalance or justify the need for adjustment. This is standard practice in observational studies.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add Table 1 showing demographic and clinical characteristics (age, severity, and outcome) stratified by group, with appropriate summary statistics.

acceptedFindings.title: Model diagnostics not reported in manuscript
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: ANCOVA relies on assumptions of normality, homoscedasticity, and absence of influential points. Although diagnostics exist in companion files, the manuscript must describe and discuss them.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a paragraph or table summarizing residual diagnostics (Shapiro‑Wilk p‑value, maximum leverage, maximum Cook’s distance, VIF) and state that assumptions were met.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Diagnostics in stats-run/diagnostics.json show Shapiro p=0.79, max leverage 0.052, max Cook’s d 0.054, max VIF 1.35; none of this appears in the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing data not quantified or discussed
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The analysis uses 240 complete cases, but the original sample size, pattern of missingness, and any potential for informative missingness are unreported. This threatens validity.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the initial number of records, how many were excluded and why, and perform a sensitivity analysis (e.g., pattern‑mixture model or multiple imputation) if missingness is non‑trivial.

acceptedFindings.title: No literature context
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The study lacks any reference to prior work on the relationship between the group and outcome, or the role of the covariates. This prevents situating the findings.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review citing relevant studies, and discuss how the current results align or contrast with existing evidence.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is unbound and exploratory, but claims imply confirmatory strength
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Unbound analyses have inflated false-positive risk; the manuscript's 'interpretable local evidence' statement is overconfident.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Bind the analysis to a pre-registered specification or downgrade all claims to explicitly exploratory language, acknowledging inflated Type I error.

acceptedFindings.title: Contradictory statements about missing artifacts and estimates
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript says 'No reader-facing paper/manuscript artifact' and 'No estimate-like records', yet both exist; this undermines trust in the report's accuracy.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove or correct these limitations statements after verifying that the manuscript reflects the actual artifacts.

acceptedFindings.title: No participant flow or baseline characteristics reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis may be biased; without details on initial cohort, exclusions, and group demographics, selection bias and generalizability cannot be assessed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a STROBE flow diagram and a table of baseline characteristics by group, comparing complete-case to excluded records.

acceptedFindings.title: Reference category for group not specified
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The group variable has three levels (likely control, enhanced, standard) but the reference is unnamed, making the reported contrasts ambiguous.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the reference category in the Methods and in footnotes of result tables.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: VIF terms in diagnostics.json include 'group_enhanced' and 'group_standard', implying a third reference level, but manuscript never names it.

acceptedFindings.title: Statistical method is described vaguely
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Reproducibility requires a clear statement of the model; readers should not need to infer from artifacts.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state: ANCOVA with outcome_cont as dependent variable, group as a three-level factor, and age and severity as covariates, using type III SS.

acceptedFindings.title: No effect sizes or clinical significance reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: P-values alone do not convey magnitude of effects; readers cannot judge practical importance.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report partial eta-squared for each effect (sum_sq_effect / (sum_sq_effect + sum_sq_residual)).

acceptedFindings.title: No literature context or references provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The study lacks scientific framing; readers cannot gauge importance or compare with prior work.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a brief background with references or explicitly state this is an internal-only analysis.
